content: The test image shows a young soybean seedling completely collapsed/wilted at the soil line on sandy soil — classic damping off appearance. The stem has lost structural integrity near the soil surface and leaves are dead/curling. Top candidates: **Pythium_damping_off**, **Rhizoctonia**, **Phytophthora**.

**Analysis:**

The test image shows a young soybean seedling (cotyledon/early trifoliate stage) that has completely collapsed and wilted onto the sandy soil. Key features:
- Complete wilt/collapse of the whole plant
- Plant is prostrate on sandy soil
- Leaves are brown and dead, stem appears to have failed at the base
- Sandy, dry-looking soil conditions

**Comparison with references:**
- **Pythium_damping_off**: Reference shows even younger/smaller seedlings barely emerged — pre/post-emergence collapse at a much earlier stage
- **Phytophthora**: Reference shows very similar complete collapse of young seedlings, brown wilted plants lying on soil — strong match
- **Rhizoctonia**: Shows reddish-brown dry lesions at soil line with plants that may be stunted but not fully collapsed
- **Sudden_death_syndrome**: Mature plants with interveinal chlorosis — not matching
- **Charcoal_Rot**: Mature stems with gray/charcoal pith — not matching

The test image most closely matches **Phytophthora** — complete seedling damping off with collapse from stem rot at the soil line, characteristic of Phytophthora root and stem rot in early-season seedlings.
